items.title: Anthropic Releases Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 With Tiered Access
items.summary: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 on November 9. Fable 5.2 is generally available through the API at $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens, with strengthened cybersecurity and biological safeguards. Mythos 5.2, which improves coding, reasoning and vision, is restricted to verified organisations in those fields via Anthropic's cyber and life-sciences verification programs. Both share an underlying model, extending the company's approach of separating broad availability from vetted access to sensitive capabilities.
items.impact: Tiered access separates general availability from vetted, sensitive-capability use — a template for responsible frontier-model distribution. The pricing also signals the intensifying margin war among leading AI labs.

items.title: Google Opens Gemini 4 Carbon to Paying Developers and Publishes Safety Report
items.summary: Google opened Gemini 4 Carbon to all paying developers and enterprises through its API at an introductory price set to expire on November 30, and published a dedicated Carbon safety report. The report carries forward the findings from Gemini 4 Argon, including Google's assessment that it cannot rule out the model reaching its critical cyber and biological capability levels without out-of-model safeguards. Carbon had earlier been limited to a subset of cyber defenders before this broader rollout.
items.impact: Broader access to a frontier model with documented critical-risk potential raises the stakes for deployment controls, third-party safeguards and ongoing safety monitoring.

items.title: Ivanti Connect Secure Zero-Day Chain Added to CISA KEV After Active Exploitation
items.summary: Ivanti shipped fixes for two more zero-days — CVE-2026-111357 (CVSS 8.8 missing-authentication privilege escalation) and CVE-2026-118527 (predictable-identifier file upload) — that were chained with the October authentication-bypass flaw CVE-2026-104935 by actor UTA0576 to achieve unauthenticated root-level remote code execution on Connect Secure VPN appliances. CISA added both new flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog; the federal remediation deadline for CVE-2026-118527 was November 13. Organisations that applied only the mid-October patch remain exposed.
items.impact: Edge VPN appliances remain prime attack targets. Organisations that patched only the October fix stay vulnerable to full takeover — immediate updates and credential rotation are required.

items.title: WordPress Core TOCTOU Flaw (CVE-2026-119977) Added to CISA KEV for Unauthenticated RCE
items.summary: CISA added a WordPress core time-of-check/time-of-use (TOCTOU) race-condition vulnerability, CVE-2026-119977, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, with a remediation due date of November 6. The flaw lets unauthenticated attackers execute code on the server during the core upgrade window because of predictable, web-accessible staging paths used for full-package upgrades. The issue is addressed in WordPress 7.1.4. CISA's BOD 26-04 now requires forensic triage for affected federal assets.
items.impact: One of the world's most deployed platforms is exposed to unauthenticated RCE during routine updates, underscoring the need to patch promptly and limit web-write exposure.

items.title: California Fines FedEx $2.975M for Ignoring Global Privacy Control Opt-Out Signals
items.source: California Privacy Protection Agency (via Digital Privacy Regs)
items.summary: California's privacy agency fined Federal Express $2.975 million after finding it ran cross-context behavioral advertising while claiming it did not sell or share personal information, ignored Global Privacy Control (GPC) opt-out preference signals, and operated broken cookie controls and an opt-out request form that never reached its online trackers. Under the settlement, FedEx must inventory its tracking technologies and test its opt-out and request methods every quarter, and keep a working Do Not Sell or Share link.
items.impact: The enforcement gives real teeth to universal opt-out signals. Businesses that fail to honor GPC now face fines plus ongoing, audited compliance obligations.
